table.ruleA: Add the cycle's feed charge to each chamber; holding limit not enforced
table.ruleB: Add row k, column i of the input table to x_i; box bound not enforced

table.ruleA: Chambers in order 1..6, sequential (chamber n's excess is already in n+1 before n+1 is checked); if mass > holding limit, excess goes to next chamber and the mass is set to the limit; chamber 6's excess goes to waste; at or below the limit, nothing happens
table.ruleB: Gauss-Seidel sweep 1..6 using values already updated in the sweep; if x_i > c_i, v = x_i - c_i goes to i+1 and x_i is set to c_i; component 6's v goes to s; at or below the bound, nothing happens

table.ruleA: Read after step 2: LARVAL with mass >= pupation mark becomes PUPAL; PUPAL with mass <= return mark becomes LARVAL; otherwise no change; at most one change per cycle; each change recorded
table.ruleB: Read after Step 2: INACTIVE with x_i >= u_i becomes ACTIVE; ACTIVE with x_i <= d_i becomes INACTIVE; otherwise no change; at most one change per iteration; each change recorded

table.ruleA: Amounts are computed at the same time from the mass at the start of the step, using the stage after step 3: LARVAL gives floor(m/4), which goes to waste; PUPAL gives floor(m/2), which is reabsorbed into the PREVIOUS chamber n-1 (chamber 1's goes to waste); the limit is not enforced
table.ruleB: Same simultaneous computation: INACTIVE gives floor(x/4), which goes to s; ACTIVE gives floor(x/2), which is added to the NEXT component i+1 (component 6's goes to s); the bound is not enforced
table.difference: The PUPAL/ACTIVE amount goes in opposite directions. A sends it upstream to n-1, and at the line edge chamber 1 loses it to waste. B sends it downstream to i+1, and at the line edge component 6 loses it to s.

table.ruleA: Sum all six masses; if the total is strictly more than 38, every chamber is halved (rounded down), the removed mass goes to waste and the cycle is recorded; a total of 38 or less does nothing (equality does not trigger it); applies to all six chambers
table.ruleB: 1-norm of x; if strictly more than 38, every x_i becomes floor(x_i/2), the removed amount goes to s and the iteration is recorded; 38 or less does nothing; applies to all six components

table.ruleA: (a) end masses 1-6, (b) end stages, (c) stage changes (cycle, chamber, before, after), (d) moult cycles, (e) waste tally, (f) balance check
table.ruleB: (a) end x_1..x_6, (b) end flags, (c) flag changes (iteration, component, before, after), (d) penalty iterations, (e) s, (f) balance check

result.probeWhy: The probe isolates the step 4 direction. Only the two edge positions, 1 and 6, start loaded, and both cross their upper mark in cycle 1. Every other position is empty and nothing is fed in. In A, position 1's half-share leaves the line and position 6's half-share flows back into position 5. In B, position 1's half-share flows forward into position 2 and position 6's half-share leaves the line. The totals stay at 38 or below, so the halving never fires and cannot mask the result. Any other difference would also show up here. The end quantities are mirrored: A gives [3,0,0,0,3,2] and B gives [3,3,0,0,0,2]. That points straight at the direction rule.
result.differingRule: In step 4, A moves a PUPAL chamber's half-share to the previous chamber (n-1), and chamber 1's goes to waste; B moves an ACTIVE component's half-share to the next component (i+1), and component 6's goes to slack.
result.trust: The two routes agree. The table found the direction difference in step 4 and showed every other rule matches. The probe confirms it in isolation: the end quantities come out mirrored ([3,0,0,0,3,2] for A, [3,3,0,0,0,2] for B), while the state changes, halving cycles and loss tally stay identical. The printed tables also give different results (A: halving in cycles 1 and 4, loss 76; B: halving in cycles 1, 4 and 5, loss 95). The arithmetic was done with a Python script, C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P13\sim.py, and the probe's cycle 1 was also checked by hand. The balance check (start + inputs = end + loss) holds on all four runs.
